newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Taiwanese foreign minister visits Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Taiwanese foreign minister visits Indonesia.

text.p: Taiwanese Foreign Minister John Chang will meet his Indonesian counterpart Ali Alatas later on Wednesday during a private one-day visit to Jakarta, Indonesian foreign ministry sources said.

The sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Chang arrived late on Tuesday and was scheduled to leave on Wednesday. The private visit was not announced officially and Chang's office in Taipei refused to comment on his whereabouts.
The Indonesian foreign ministry sources said no agenda was fixed for the meeting with Alatas.

The visit is likely to anger Beijing, which views Taiwan as a renegade province and routinely attacks the island's attempts to raise its international profile. A civil war separated China and Taiwan in 1949.
Indonesia and Taiwan do not have diplomatic relations but have strong business ties.
Taiwan's mass-circulation United Daily News newspaper reported Chang would discuss economic and trade ties between the two countries in his talks with Alatas.
It said also he would attend the wedding of Alatas' daughter, but the ceremony was scheduled for this weekend.
Chang's unannounced trip to Indonesia followed Vice-President Lien Chan's secret visit to the Ukraine in late August.
Beijing bitterly protested that visit and cancelled a visit by a high-level Chinese delegation to Kiev after Lien, who doubles as premier, went there to promote unofficial ties.
Beijing accused the former Soviet republic of violating the "one China" commitment that it made in establishing ties with Beijing.
Only 30 countries, mostly in Africa and central America, recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government.
Taiwan, maintaining that its 21 million people have a right to a voice in the United Nations and other forums, has pushed to win new foreign friends and raise its international profile.

Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui made an unofficial visit to Jakarta in February 1994. China, which has diplomatic relations with Indonesia, was enraged by the visit and lodged an official protest with Jakarta.
